key_insight: An imposed magnetic field shifts 2D Rayleigh-Bénard convection toward more frequent traveling-roll dynamics and promotes roll splitting, indicating a pathway from coherent convection to chaotic/turbulent behavior.
engineering_relevance: Magnetic-field control can be used to modulate convective stability and structure in electro- and magnetohydrodynamic systems where suppressing or triggering flow transition matters.
method: Numerical simulation of two-dimensional Rayleigh-Bénard convection
Compare hydrodynamic baseline with cases under an external background magnetic field
Analyze flow topology, roll dynamics, and vortex/reconnection events
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a baseline hydrodynamic regime with traveling rolls, an attractor-merging crisis leading to chaotic traveling rolls, and intermittent magnetic reconnection coincident with saddle-center collisions and roll splitting under magnetic forcing.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on 2D simulations, so extension to realistic 3D convection and parameter sensitivity should be checked before applying the mechanism broadly.
paper_title: Transition to chaos in two-dimensional Rayleigh-Bénard convection: the role of the magnetic field
